answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents mint unique identities staked with rare assets—like saffron reserves, velvet guild bonds, or an opal treasury stake. Each agent verifies its lineage through cryptographic attestation chains and privacy-preserving zero-knowledge proofs. When coordinating in clusters, recursive verification imposes an exponential capital exhaustion curve, making the cost of sustaining a malicious Sybil swarm scale superlinearly.
